name: web_search
description:
Unified web search + research. search_only=true (default false) is a pure provider search across engines (duckduckgo/google/bing/exa/browser) returning a deduped list. search_only=false also fetches up to depth candidate pages, returning one record per source with status, markdown, and provenance for a cited synthesis. When fetching, use_smart selects the render strategy.

Args:
    query: The search query / research topic
    search_only: true returns only provider search results; false also fetches up to depth pages and returns per-source records.
    max_results: Maximum number of search results to consider (default: 5).
    depth: Number of candidate pages to fetch when search_only=false (default: 5).
    max_tokens: Global token budget for the whole response (0 = toolbox default).
    provider: Search engine to prefer, in both modes. search_only=false plans the research run through this provider. Falls back through other providers on failure.
    use_smart: Render strategy for fetched pages: 'auto' (default; follows fetch_mode), 'browser' (stealth browser first, static fallback), or 'static' (never renders). Ignored when search_only=true.

name: inspect_html_page
description:
Fetch and extract markdown content from a web page. Set use_smart='browser' for JS-rendered pages (SPA, anti-bot); 'auto' (default) follows fetch_mode; 'static' is static-only. If the page exceeds the output budget, pass the research query to keep only the most relevant sections, or offset / max_chunks to page through it in chunks. Returns markdown, follow-up links, and provenance.

Args:
    url: The URL to inspect
    use_smart: Render strategy: 'auto' (default), 'browser' (headless browser first, static on failure), or 'static'.
    query: The research query. When the page exceeds the output budget, only the most relevant sections are returned.
    offset: Character offset into the page markdown to start from; pass the previous call's next_offset to resume.
    max_chunks: Number of consecutive budget-sized chunks to return (each chunk respects the output budget; the total may exceed it).
    structured: true returns a structured payload (metadata, tables, links) instead of raw markdown.

name: download_file
description:
Download a remote file to an explicit local path without requiring document extraction. Streams under the configured/per-call byte cap, follows and revalidates redirects, respects robots.txt and SSRF protections, and validates PDF magic when expected_format='pdf' or the output ends in .pdf. Existing destinations are preserved unless overwrite=true. Optional fallback_urls are caller-supplied OA/repository candidates tried sequentially; every URL is checked independently and bot walls are never bypassed.

Args:
    source: Remote HTTP(S) URL to download
    output_path: Local destination file path
    min_bytes: Minimum accepted file size in bytes (default: 1).
    max_bytes: Maximum bytes (0 uses the configured max_response_bytes cap).
    expected_format: 'auto' validates PDF when output_path ends in .pdf; 'pdf' always validates the %PDF- signature.
    overwrite: Replace an existing destination only when true.
    resume: Continue an existing partial file with Range/If-Range; servers that ignore Range restart the file.
    fallback_urls: Optional caller-supplied ordered OA/repository mirrors to try sequentially after the primary URL; every candidate still obeys robots/SSRF checks.

name: locate_pdf
description:
Resolve a DOI through OpenAlex (plus Unpaywall v2 when GOSSAMER_UNPAYWALL_EMAIL is configured) and return inspectable open-access PDF or landing-page candidates with source/license/version provenance. This locates but does not download; use download_file separately. Returns not_found, closed_access, open_access, or a top-level error status.

Args:
    doi: Bare DOI, doi: prefixed value, or https://doi.org/ resolver URL

name: extract_document
description:
Extract text content from documents via URL or local path: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, plus text formats (TXT, MD, CSV, JSON, XML) and RSS/Atom feeds. For large documents, pass pages (e.g. '10-20') to read a page range instead of the whole file.

Args:
    source: URL or local file path to the document
    pages: 1-based inclusive page range for PDFs ('10', '10-20', '10-', '-20'); for XLSX the range selects sheets. Omitted -> the whole document.
    structured: true returns a validated ParsedDocumentPayload (metadata, pages, tables) as JSON instead of plain text.
    store: true writes the original bytes and the full extracted text to disk under store_dir; the result includes a 'stored' object with paths and sizes. Cannot combine with pages=.
    store_dir: Directory to write stored files into (created if missing). Only used when store=true.
    include_images: PDF only; requires store=true. Also extract embedded raster images into <stem>.files/ with a ## Figures section (reported under stored.resources). Vector-only figures are skipped; tables render by default.
    tables_as: Rendering of spreadsheet (XLSX) tables in the returned content: 'json' (default; array of {sheet, headers, rows}), 'markdown' (pipe tables), or 'csv' (comma-separated, one ## <sheet> block per sheet). Other formats keep markdown rendering.
    prefer_jats: JATS-first scholarly route (default true): DOI-resolvable sources try publisher full-text XML (EuropePMC, then PLOS) via the in-house _core JATS kernel before the PDF path. pages= with a JATS-resolvable source errors; structured=true or tables_as != 'markdown' skips the route.

name: discover_resources
description:
Discover a site's structured resources without crawling the link graph (Tier 3.12). Finds feed declarations (<link rel=alternate> RSS/Atom/Feed-JSON) on the page and probes the site root for /sitemap.xml, following bounded sitemap indexes. Returns deduplicated, budgeted lists of feed URLs and sitemap page URLs.

Args:
    url: A page or site URL to discover resources for

url.description: A page or site URL to discover resources for
url.title: Url

name: crawl
description:
Relevance-ranked crawl of a URL's link graph (cross-domain by default) to find the pages most relevant to a query. Walks from root_url, scoring candidates by query relevance that decays with depth, so the page budget lands on the most relevant links. Optionally seed with a site-scoped search (search_prior) and/or extra URLs (seed_urls). Returns per page: title, relevance score, and a short skim; plus unfetched document links and skipped links. Full pages stay cached for later re-reads.

Args:
    root_url: Seed URL to start the traversal from
    query: Relevance focus for the frontier ranking. When omitted, the root page's own title and content words stand in for it.
    max_depth: Maximum link hops from the root (0 = root only; hard cap 5)
    max_pages: Total pages fetched across all depths (1-50); failed fetches do not count
    same_host: When true, follow only links on the root's host (www. ignored); false follows external links too
    min_score: Minimum relevance score for a candidate to enter the frontier (0 = follow everything that passes the boilerplate filters)
    excerpts: Also return a keyword-densest 300-char excerpt per page (raises the payload size; pair with a lower max_pages)
    search_prior: Before traversing, run one site-scoped web search and feed its top results into the frontier at depth 1 (exempt from min_score; a failed search is non-fatal)
    seed_urls: Extra starting URLs, pushed at depth 0 (children at depth 1); they respect min_score
    use_smart: Render strategy for crawled pages: 'auto' (default), 'browser' (headless first), or 'static'.

name: manage_cache
description:
Unified cache maintenance. action='clear' wipes the memory and disk caches plus the visited-URL set (force fresh fetches); action='prune' (default) removes expired entries and evicts to the size cap while keeping valid ones; action='reset' forgets visited URLs without clearing caches (retry a failed page).

Args:
    action: Cache operation: 'clear' (wipe caches + visited), 'prune' (default, evict expired/LRU to size cap), or 'reset' (forget visited URLs only).

action.description: Cache operation: 'clear' (wipe caches + visited), 'prune' (default, evict expired/LRU to size cap), or 'reset' (forget visited URLs only).

name: research_by_category
description:
Category-aware, provider-specific search. Classifies the query into a domain category (scholarly, legal, patent, financial, geo, general) and calls that category's default provider. Omit the query to return the full taxonomy (category descriptions and provider ids) as JSON. Pass provider=<id> to call a specific source; pass category=<name> to skip classification. No automatic fallback between providers -- the caller chooses. Pass providers=[...] for an explicit scholarly multi-search merged by DOI/arXiv ID. OpenAlex-only filter/select/title/author options pass through to that API. Returns the chosen category, provider, and results as JSON. Provider failures keep results as an empty list and add a top-level error field.

Args:
    query: The search query. Omit it to return the full category -> provider taxonomy as JSON instead, so you can discover which provider to use.
    category: Optional category to use directly (e.g. 'scholarly', 'legal', 'financial', 'geo', 'general'); skips classification. Pair with provider= to pick a source within it.
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    provider: Optional provider id to call (see the taxonomy from a no-query call). Given alone, its owning category is used; with category= it must belong to that category. Omitted -> the category's default provider. No automatic fallback.
    filter: OpenAlex-native filter expression; valid only with provider='openalex'.
    select: OpenAlex-native comma-separated field projection; valid only with provider='openalex'.
    title: OpenAlex title search; maps to verified title.search filter. Valid only with provider='openalex'.
    author: OpenAlex author search; maps to verified raw_author_name.search filter. Valid only with provider='openalex'.
    providers: Explicit providers for sequential scholarly search/merge, e.g. ['openalex', 'arxiv']. Mutually exclusive with provider= and supported only for scholarly.

name: export_citations
description:
Reconstruct and export citations from search results. Pass a list of DOIs, URLs, or JSON-serialized adapter result dicts; returns them formatted as bibtex (default), csl-json, apa, or mla. DOIs and URLs are resolved via the scholarly adapters (openalex, crossref, arxiv, pubmed, doaj).

Args:
    results: List of DOIs ('10.xxxx/...'), URLs, or JSON-serialized adapter result dicts to cite.
    style: Citation style: bibtex, csl-json, apa, or mla.
    enrich: When true, make one canonical DOI lookup per unique DOI to fill in a missing venue/abstract.
    dedupe: Collapse records that share a DOI or URL before formatting.
    from_pdf: Treat every string input as a local PDF path and cite its detected DOI; PDFs without a DOI return an error.

name: check_sources
description:
Probe whether source URLs are reachable without downloading their pages (Workstream 2). Takes a list of URLs (strings or {url} dicts), validates each through the SSRF guard, runs a lightweight status probe per URL (polite / parallel / bounded), and returns per-URL status: ok (2xx/3xx), unreachable (4xx/5xx), blocked (SSRF), or error (network/timeout). Reuses the shared fetch pipeline -- no new HTTP surface.

Args:
    urls: List of URLs to probe (plain strings or {url} dicts).
    mode: Probe mode: 'status' (HEAD/minimal GET, default) or 'content' (full fetch).
